candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is CPVT, a distinct channelopathy triggered by adrenergic stimulation (consistent with the noisy/stressful environment precipitating VF in a young woman with no structural heart disease and a normal QTc of 380 ms). Long QT Syndrome, acquired, is a different channelopathy mechanism requiring QTc prolongation; the ECG here explicitly shows a normal QTc (380 ms), making LQTS incompatible. While both are channelopathies causing malignant arrhythmia, they are distinct diagnostic entities with conflicting electrophysiological subtypes.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Long QT Syndrome (acquired) vs. Catecholaminergic Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia (CPVT)

case_quality_flags: Normal QTc (380 ms) and stress/catecholamine-triggered VF in a young woman with no structural disease strongly supports CPVT over any LQTS variant
Risperidone use could suggest drug-induced QTc prolongation, but the measured QTc is normal, further undermining acquired LQTS
